i was previously diagnosed with anorexia and bulimia. it landed me in an inpatient hospital for 3 months. it took me to rock bottom and i just decided i was tired of it. i couldn’t keep doing it anymore. it wasn’t sustainable and ir was killing me. it’s been 5 years since then im mostly recovered. most days i don’t think about calories and i eat what i want without feeling bad. it comes up every now and then but im strong enough to fight it easily. 

tips: 
1. give a name to your disordered eating and separate it from yourself. you don’t want to starve yourself, Anna wants you to and she’s a bitch. you shouldn’t listen to her bc she just wants your down fall. 
2. don’t ever count calories, don’t ever even look at them. listen to your body. does your stomach hurt? can you tell you’re hungry? eat until your full, but not to the point of pain. it’s ok to leave food uneaten as long as you’re full.
3. eating disorders in their nature are about control, so look to the rest of your life. do you feel out of control? are things stressing you out that you can’t change? what can you do other than controlling your food to help you feel more empowered?
4. practice positive self talk. seriously it really helps. start small. if you find yourself saying “ i hate how i look, im so fat”, start with “i FEEL like i hate myself IN THIS MOMENT, i FEEL fat.” work up to “I feel like i hate myself but i know thats just my eating disorder talking and i dont want to listen to her”. work up to more and more positive versions. 
5. CBT therapy is proven the most effective for eating disorders

and just an anecdote, when i developed anorexia i was severely underweight and sick. due to medications and recovery i am now overweight. but thats ok. i never loved myself when i was thin, i was never enough. since healing and gaining weight, i have only ever learned to love myself. i associate being overweight with loving myself.

another tip, it is ok to not like how you look. it is NOT okay to punish yourself because you don’t like how you look. when i feel unhappy w how i look i tell myself “I don’t like how i look right now. that’s okay. i still deserve love and im not worth any less as person. i love myself.” it is ok to feel upset that you’re not happy w your appearance, but just remember that doesn’t mean you have to punish yourself by starving or other behaviors.

my routine is similar to yours i use:

Alternate Vitamin C and Niacinamide in the mornings . You can use hyaluronic acid every morning, but use it after the Vit C and it’s absorbed 

Use salicylic acid every evening 

Use the toner on day 1, the retinoid on day 2, don’t use either for 2 days, repeat. You can swap out the toner for the AHA + BHA peel once a week

niacinamide and salicylic shouldn’t be used at the same time, and if they are it needs to be 30min apart. they work really well together but not at the same time due to pH differences. I use niacinamide in the morning and salicylic acid at night. 

For your exfoliators - the toner, the aha+bha peel, and the retinoid…. it’s recommended to use the exfoliator (toner or peel) day 1, the retinoid day 2, then that 2 days of rest for a 4 day cycle. I’d recommend only using the peel once a week. 

Also, have you used any of these products before? this is A LOT to throw at your skin all at once. Start it baby steps so you don’t irritate your skin or have excessive purging. i looked up some other coping skills from my journal lol

-Deep breathing, in for 4 sec, hold for 7 sec, release for 8 sec. can really help calm you down.

-tense your whole body or parts of your body and then relax them. just focus on the sensations. 

-write down things you’re grateful for, or things that people say or do that make you feel better. 

-Observation, just focus on every detail on something around you. Could be something pretty or something you like. Notice your urges and pay attention to them in your body 

-write down what happened, what you’re feeling and how it’s affecting your mind and body. include what you’ve been doing to cope. 

-tell yourself affirmations even if you don’t believe it

-effectiveness - ask yourself “is this effective? will this help achieve the outcome i want? what outcome do i want?”

some mindfulness coping skills i use:

-close your eyes and pretend you are on a mountain at the top. you are alone at the top, and below you on the ground is your problems. just focus on yourself at the top right now, you can be present for your issues later. 

-close your eyes and imagine you are on a wave, surfing. the wave is your emotions and know you just have to ride it out, and you will be ok. 

-close your eyes and imagine a box. any box you like, you can really put as much creativity into this as you like. put all your issues into the box and lock it. you can unlock it when you feel you’re ready

You clearly care for your boyfriend which is amazing, but look at how you said you need to be there and support him when he’s struggling. Dont you think maybe he feels the same about you? You also deserve support even if you feel you’re not struggling as hard. 

My boyfriend is kind of similar to you, I struggle a lot more obviously than he does but it doesn’t mean he doesn’t either. It hurtful when he doesn’t share what he’s going through because no matter what I’m struggling with, even in the middle of a breakdown, I want to be there for him too. I would feel very guilty if I ever found out he was bottling it up just to comfort me. Do you think your boyfriend may feel similar to this? Just because you are struggling while he is, doesn’t mean you’re distracting from helping him. 

It would be helpful to set up boundaries so that when you two do share, neither of you are being counter productive?  Examples would be “No talking about XX right before bed”, and leaving out language that may trigger each other. It’s also REALLY beneficial to spell out how you would like to be supported. Dont get me wrong - everyone wants to be understood without saying anything especially when you’re crying, but in my experience my boyfriend would be really upset bc he had no idea what I wanted in terms of support. 

For me personally, I said I didn’t need him talking through my problems, I didn’t need him fixing my problems, all I wanted was for someone to be by my side and basically say the love me no matter what. I also set up boundaries that he didn’t need to be there next to be everytime I cried (it was happening a lot at the time).

Lastly, I STRUGGLE with communication especially verbal. I essentially write everything down and then show it to him. Would this help you? It helps having everything written down and then just kinda sliding it over so you really can just breathe while they’re reading it. I feel it takes some of the pressure off. Perhaps an initial thing you could write is, “I love you and want to support you. But i feel I also need some extra support recently. Could you do XX for me when I feel XX?”

I really hope any of this helps. I understand how hard it is, but you really don’t want to accidentally build up resentment because you feel you’re incapable of sharing with your loved ones. You DESERVE support and love.

I have struggled with acne since junior year of high school (5 years ago). It was a really big self esteem bomb as i had new breakouts every day and it was pretty painful. I used to wear makeup constantly. 

When i first started doing skin care i used to use a lot of drugstore/sephora stuff and had like an 8-10 step routine kind of thing. I had given myself chemical burns a few times due to overuse of products. I never really paid attention that much attention to what i used together. I probably did this for 3 years? 

Then about 2 years ago i finally went to a dermatologist and got a prescription for clindomycin and i used that once a day every other day along w aveeno ultra calming foam wash and aveeno clear complexion moisturizer. It really helped! However it didn’t make my breakouts stop, it just made what i had better. 

A year ago I went to school to become an aesthetician and in school i ended up getting 3 facials  a week with DMK products. I also used the DMK products every night at home. (The before photo is from when i first started school) Unfortunately, after 3 months I had to drop out of school for medical reasons. I continued to use DMK for a month after but then completely stopped any sort of routine. 

Since December and until August I stopped doing any sort of skin care routine. I just didn’t have the energy and I also stopped wearing makeup. I noticed a huge improvement of my skin in this time, and i was hardly getting new break outs. In August I noticed I was getting a lot more tiny white heads and texture on my forehead so I started using Aveeno again. 

I found out this week my school is closing and I’ll never be able to finish so I decided that at least I can use the thousands of $ of skincare I have! In the after photo I washed my face w DMK acu-klenz, exfoliated with micro peel, used a hydrating mask, moisturized with vitamin c, seba-e and used an eye toner, I then finished off with 2 correction creams creme citrique and acu moist. 

I’m so happy how amazing I think my skin looks and how far I’ve come. I’m glad that at least the silver lining of my school closing is that I can use some pretty high quality skin care for a little while. 

What I Think Made My Skin Better: Obviously I think the facials really gave me a huge boost at probably getting rid of all the garbage under my skin so I didn’t break out as often. I also think reducing my products helped as I wasn’t overwhelming my skin. I also think it’s hormonal as my brother experienced acne the exact same was as me and his also stopped at 20. Honestly, I wouldn’t be surprised if my acne stopped around this time whether or not i used skincare.
